summary.grade_reason: Automatic F — red-team confirmed live breaches of critical objectives: state-machine bypass (RED-002) and 3/4 pentest objectives achieved.

findings.title: Complete Absence of Authentication on All API Endpoints
findings.description: Zero authentication middleware is configured anywhere in the application. All endpoints — including CRUD, state transitions (approve, reject, dispatch, force-approve), and webhooks — are fully public. Confirmed live by red-teamer: anonymous caller created, read, updated, and deleted arbitrary items via curl with no credentials.
findings.evidence: RED-001: GET /api/feature-requests → 200 no auth. POST /api/feature-requests → 201 Created. DELETE /api/feature-requests/FR-0005 → 204.
findings.remediation: Add JWT authentication middleware in app.ts applied globally before all /api/* routes. Exempt only /health. Gate approve/reject/dispatch/force-approve behind a `reviewer` or `admin` role. For webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.

findings.title: State Machine Bypass — Force-Approve Skips All Human Review
findings.description: The /force-approve and overrideRoute:fast-track paths allow any unauthenticated caller to bypass the entire assessment pipeline and set an item to 'approved' with zero votes and zero human review. Confirmed live: item FR-0001 reached approved status with votes:[] in 3 anonymous requests.
findings.remediation: Require authenticated admin/reviewer role for force-approve and overrideRoute. PATCH status must enforce the same state machine transitions as dedicated action endpoints. Never allow arbitrary status values via PATCH.

findings.title: Dependency Gating Bypass — PATCH blocked_by:[] Clears Blockers Without Authorization
findings.description: PATCH /api/work-items/:id with blocked_by:[] silently strips all dependency blockers regardless of item status. An attacker can clear blockers on an approved-but-blocked item and then advance it to dispatched — bypassing dependency resolution. Confirmed live: FR-0028 advanced to approved with FR-0029 still unresolved.
findings.evidence: RED-003: FR-0028 pending_dependencies → PATCH blocked_by:[] → approved. FR-0029 still in 'potential'.
findings.remediation: Clearing blockers must only be possible via the /dependencies endpoint with proper resolution semantics (not via a free field patch). State transitions away from pending_dependencies must re-validate has_unresolved_blockers server-side, not trust the cached field.

findings.title: Unbounded Pagination — Full Dataset Enumeration via limit=999999
findings.description: The limit query parameter has no upper cap. Any unauthenticated caller can request limit=999999 and receive the entire dataset in a single response. Negative page values and NaN limit also bypass pagination guards. Confirmed live: 79 items returned in a single unauthenticated request.
findings.evidence: RED-005: GET /api/feature-requests?limit=999999 → all 79 items. page=-1 also returns full dataset.
findings.remediation: Clamp limit server-side: const limit = Math.min(parseInt(...) || 20, 100). Reject negative/NaN page values with 400. Apply uniformly to all list endpoints.

findings.title: Rejection Cascade Triggers Unintended Auto-Dispatch of Dependent Items
findings.description: POST /reject calls onItemResolved() which auto-dispatches any approved dependent item that is now unblocked. An attacker can create an item B depending on A, bring B to Approved, then reject A — triggering unintended dispatch of B with no human action on B's dispatch.
findings.remediation: The rejection cascade auto-dispatch should require explicit human confirmation. Add a dispatch_gating_override flag or gate cascade dispatch behind the same role check as direct dispatch.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Webhook Endpoints — No HMAC Signature Verification
findings.description: Both /api/intake/zendesk and /api/intake/automated accept unauthenticated POST requests with no HMAC-SHA256 verification. Any external actor can spoof Zendesk events and inject arbitrary work items indistinguishable from legitimate submissions. Rate-limiting absence allows flooding.
findings.remediation: Verify X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature HMAC-SHA256 using a shared secret from environment variables. For automated intake require a bearer token. Reject with 401 on verification failure.

findings.title: No Role-Based Access Control on Privileged State Transitions
findings.description: Beyond the authentication gap (F-001), there is no concept of roles. Once authentication is added, approve/reject/dispatch endpoints must still be gated by role (reviewer/manager). Without RBAC any authenticated user can perform privileged operations.
findings.remediation: After implementing authentication, introduce a role-check middleware. approve/reject/dispatch require reviewer or manager role. Centralize enforcement in middleware, not duplicated per-handler.

findings.title: No TLS — All API Traffic Travels in Plaintext
findings.description: The Express server binds to plain HTTP on port 3001. All API traffic including state transitions and work item content is transmitted in cleartext. The Vite dev proxy also proxies to http://localhost:3001.
findings.remediation: Enforce HTTPS at the infrastructure layer via Nginx/Caddy with TLS. Add HTTP→HTTPS redirect middleware for production. Replace Vite dev proxy with reverse-proxy TLS termination in production.

findings.title: Unvalidated Enum Inputs via Intake Routes — Data Integrity Bypass
findings.description: Intake webhook endpoints pass body.type and body.priority to createWorkItem() without enum validation. An attacker can store arbitrary strings as type/priority values, corrupting routing logic that switches on item.type. The regular /api/work-items POST endpoint validates these fields correctly — intake bypasses that guard.
findings.remediation: Add enum validation in both intake handlers identical to the pattern in workItems.ts POST handler. Validate body.type against Object.values(WorkItemType) before storing.

findings.title: Soft-Deleted Item ID Leak via Dependency Response (Partial IDOR)
findings.description: Soft-deleted items are correctly 404'd on direct GET, but their internal IDs leak via the blocked_by array of dependent items. has_unresolved_blockers: true persists indefinitely on items blocked by a deleted resource (can never auto-resolve). Confirmed live: FR-0005 ID leaked in FR-0006 response after deletion.
findings.remediation: When a blocker is soft-deleted, cascade-resolve or cascade-remove its dependency links. Filter soft-deleted blockers from the blocked_by response array.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting — Write Flooding / Denial of Service
findings.description: No rate limiting exists on any endpoint. Confirmed live: 50 POST /api/feature-requests completed in 373ms with no throttle. Write queue can be poisoned with unlimited attacker-controlled items.
findings.remediation: Add express-rate-limit with per-IP limits (e.g., 100 req/15min global, 20 req/min for intake endpoints).

findings.title: Prometheus /metrics Endpoint Unauthenticated — Operational Intelligence Leak
findings.description: GET /metrics is publicly accessible and exposes queue depths, dispatch rates, route-level counters, and error rates. Also reveals prior attack attempt counts (force-approve 409s). Confirmed live: full Prometheus metrics page returned without credentials.
findings.evidence: RED-007: feature_request_status_transitions_total, pipeline_stage_completions_total exposed with no auth.
findings.remediation: Restrict /metrics to internal network via firewall/ingress rule, or add bearer-token check using process.env.METRICS_TOKEN.

findings.title: Internal Error Messages and Service URLs Leaked to Clients
findings.description: Raw err.message forwarded in 500 responses in workflow.ts. Confirmed live: GET /api/orchestrator/ returns {"error":"Orchestrator unreachable at http://localhost:8080"} — disclosing internal service URL and port.
findings.remediation: Return generic 'Internal server error' to clients; keep detail in server logs only. Replace verbose proxy errors with 'Service temporarily unavailable'.

findings.title: Required Audit Events Missing from Logging Layer
findings.description: login_attempt, permission_denied, and data_export audit events are entirely absent. state_transition is logged as an info message but not as a structured audit event with actor identity. Unachievable until authentication (F-001) is resolved.
findings.remediation: Add structured audit event emitter tagging entries with event_type, actor, and resource_id. Implement after authentication is in place.

findings.title: Audit Logs Lack Actor Identity
findings.description: Every log entry records what happened but not who did it. The agent field in change history is hardcoded to 'user' or 'system'. Without actor identity, audit trails are non-compliant for SOC2 accountability requirements.
findings.remediation: Inject authenticated user ID into request context via AsyncLocalStorage. Pass to buildChangeEntry and all logger calls.

findings.title: No Persistent Storage — Data Lost on Restart, No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: All work item data is stored in a JavaScript Map in process memory. Any process restart loses all data. No database, no disk persistence, no encryption at rest. Audit logs are stdout-only (ephemeral). Fails SOC2 durability and encryption-at-rest controls.
findings.remediation: Migrate to PostgreSQL with ACID compliance and encryption at rest. Persist audit logs to a write-once append log or dedicated audit table.

findings.title: No Hard Delete — GDPR Right to Erasure Not Supported
findings.description: Only soft delete exists (sets deleted:true). No mechanism to permanently remove data. If work items contain personal data (submitter name, email), this violates GDPR Art. 17.
findings.remediation: Add hardDelete() function and DELETE /api/work-items/:id/purge endpoint restricted to admin role. Document retention policy (e.g., soft-deleted items purged after 90 days).

findings.title: Non-numeric Pagination Parameters Return Silent 200 with Empty Data
findings.description: parseInt('abc') returns NaN. page=abc or limit=abc causes slice(NaN,NaN) returning [] with 200 OK. Clients may treat empty data as 'no items' and stop polling. Confirmed behaviorally via RED-005 (NaN limit tested).
findings.remediation: Return 400 Bad Request for non-numeric pagination parameters. Validate and sanitize page/limit before use.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (No helmet or Equivalent)
findings.description: CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, and Referrer-Policy headers are absent. No CORS allowlist configured. Exposes frontend to clickjacking and MIME-sniffing attacks.
findings.remediation: Add helmet middleware as the first app.use() call. Configure CORS with explicit origin allowlist using the cors package.

findings.title: Orchestrator Internal Service URL Disclosed in Error Responses
findings.description: GET /api/orchestrator/ returns 'Orchestrator unreachable at http://localhost:8080' — disclosing internal hostname and port to any caller. Path traversal attempts return 404, so not exploitable beyond reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Replace verbose error with 'Service temporarily unavailable'. Remove internal URL from client-visible error responses.

findings.title: Error Message ID Enumeration via Dependency Endpoints
findings.description: Different error messages for existing vs non-existing IDs allow sequential enumeration of the entire ID space. Confirmed live: self-reference returns 'cannot depend on itself' (item exists); non-existent returns 'Item not found: FR-9999'.
findings.evidence: RED-009: FR-0001 self-reference → 400. FR-9999 → 404 'Item not found: FR-9999'.
findings.remediation: Return uniform 404 Not Found for both self-reference and non-existent blocker. Avoid verbatim internal IDs in error messages.

findings.title: Object.assign Without Prototype Guard in workItemStore
findings.description: Object.assign merges the updates parameter directly onto stored items. Current callers use an allowedFields whitelist, but one missed whitelist check away from prototype pollution. A future caller passing user-controlled data without a whitelist risks __proto__ corruption.
findings.remediation: Use spread syntax { ...item, ...updates } instead of Object.assign. Add explicit __proto__ key guard in the store.

findings.title: Unused pino Production Dependency
findings.description: pino ^8.17.0 is listed as a production dependency but never imported. Unused production dependencies unnecessarily increase the attack surface.
findings.remediation: Run npm uninstall pino. If pino was intended to replace the custom logger, complete that migration.
